caption: The stokvel payout landed this week and it's already spent on the roof and January's uniforms before I've even enjoyed it. What does your payout month actually go on?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R24 300
p/m income
Living in Empangeni
slides.body:
Female, 39
Married, three kids
Job: Quality control assistant, sugar mill
Net income: R24 300 p/m (this month, includes her annual stokvel payout)

slides.title: School fees & uniforms
slides.includes: Three kids, new uniforms, the January stock-up I usually can't afford to do early
slides.body: The payout means I don't have to choose between January's costs and December's groceries this year.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: The festive season stock-up, plus the usual monthly shop
slides.body: I buy more than usual this month on purpose. It's the one time I can.

slides.title: Roof repair
slides.includes: Patched the leak in the back room before the rains, materials and labour
slides.body: I've been waiting for this money literally all year to fix this.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: 3 bed near the mill, water, refuse
slides.body: The one bill that doesn't care whether the payout landed or not.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the mill, plus the school run when my husband's on the early shift
slides.body: Same every month, payout or not.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, funeral policy, phone & data, restarting next year's stokvel contribution, clothing account
slides.body: Five things that keep running whether or not this was a payout month.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R24 300 this month. Most months it's closer to R14 500. The payout is spoken for before it even lands.

slides.title: I finally saw the payout against the whole month
slides.body:
I uploaded this month's statement to Beyond Horizon the day the stokvel paid out, just to see it against everything else due at the same time.

Seeing the roof repair and the school fees on one screen made the number feel used well, not just spent.

No bank login needed.
